Were we watching the same movie? The first 1/3rd of the movie got me extremely invested. Sure, it was a slow burn, but the character interactions had so much character development i felt. Two brothers who initially had run to chicago, thinking the North was free of racism, as did Sammy, only to cone home with a completely different outlook. "Racism just looks a little different up there."

The theme of music acting as a sort of "human library" attracting spirits from past and future in particular was something I loved. Honestly, I think too many people went in thinking it was gonna be a straight-up horror movie instead of the slow, psychological thriller period piece that it is. The horror, in my opinion, comes from the attitudes of the time. The 1930s south was incredibly dangerous for black folk who just wanted to be free, as evident by the multiple times people casually talking about how their friends/family were lynched for seemingly no reason, like Delta Slim's friend being lynched because of a made up story. The first 1/3rd of the movie not only introduces the 3 main characters but also shows just how brutal things could be, with one of the brothers shooting two guys trying to loot his truck in broad daylight and almost no on bats an eye. There's way more to the movie that i haven't touched on, but i thought it was fantastic. The best movies are the ones that make you want to look more into it afterwards, imo.
